summary: Returns the value after checking that it is not a regular expression.
description: Identified by its internal tag rather than by `instanceof`, so a regular expression from another frame is recognised too.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, with a regular expression excluded from its type.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is a regular expression.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireNonRegExp("/a/"); // => "/a/"
requireNonRegExp({}); // => {}
requireNonRegExp(/a/); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonRegExp(new RegExp("a")); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
